details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated severe storms appear possible from mid-afternoon into this evening. Damaging wind gusts are the primary hazard. A watch issuance is not anticipated due to the limited areal coverage of the threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent thunderstorm development has occurred over the WV Panhandle, northwest of Harrisonburg, VA, amidst a moist and moderately unstable air mass with MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg. Farther east along the lee side of the Blue Ridge, visible satellite imagery indicates deepening cumulus within a low-level upslope regime. Latest time-lagged HRRR and RRFS ensemble guidance suggests that a small cluster of thunderstorms may evolve out of those areas of deepening moist convection over northern VA later this afternoon into evening. The current VWP from Charleston, WV is sampling 30-40 kt of westerly winds above 4 km AGL, which may contribute to some organization as updrafts continue to mature this afternoon. When coupled with steepening low-level lapse rates, the environment appears supportive of locally damaging wind gusts as storms progress east across the discussion area

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Scattered damaging/severe wind gusts and isolated large hail are expected across portions of the Mid South this afternoon. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered damaging/severe wind gusts and isolated large hail are expected across portions of the Mid South this afternoon. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest surface analysis depicts a west-east oriented cold front extending from far southern Illinois into southern Missouri and Kansas. Also evident in visible satellite imagery are an MCV located in close proximity to ongoing convection across far southeastern Kansas and a surface confluence zone across northern Arkansas demarcated by a zone of developing cumulus. As this MCV and surface cold front continue to progress south-southeastward through mid-afternoon, guidance suggests that ongoing convection should intensify and/or additional development will occur along the aforementioned boundaries amid a moderately unstable environment. As convective coverage increases through the mid-afternoon, enhanced mid-level flow associated with the MCV (40-50 kts sampled by the Tulsa/Wichita VWPs along the southern flank of the MCV) will aid in the organization of convection into one or more linear clusters. Scattered damaging/severe wind gusts (and potentially a few significant gusts to 75-80 mph) are likely to accompany this cluster given the enhanced mid-level flow and presence of very steep low-to-mid level lapse rates below 600 mb (as depicted by recent objective analysis and sampled by the 12 UTC LZK observed sounding). A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed in the next 1-2 hours to address this severe risk
